fixture_sha256: computed by the harness at run time, so a silently edited fixture fails loudly
_why_two_claims: AGREEMENT and RECOVERY are different claims and the library makes both, separately.
Agreement asks whether the four implementations compute the same thing. It is tight, because
given identical data any real difference is a package default, which is exactly the failure the
schema prompt warns about: 'silently different defaults are how two correct-looking
Recovery asks whether they compute the RIGHT thing. It is loose, because an estimate carries
sampling error, and its job is to catch four implementations that agree on the same wrong model.
Agreement alone would pass four identical mistakes. Recovery alone would pass a default mismatch
smaller than sampling error. Neither is sufficient and this is why.
_why_not_self_generated: expected values are NOT produced by running this library's own code and recording the output.
That is the golden-file trap this project has already documented: a golden regenerated from the
build it is meant to check passes against whatever the build produced, and pins nothing.
The truth here is independent of every implementation: the fixture generator chooses the case
within each matched set with probability proportional to exp(b1*x1 + b2*x2), which IS the
conditional likelihood clogit maximises, so the true betas are the model's own parameters.

truth.source: the fixture's data-generating process, not any implementation of the analysis

agreement.claim: every EXECUTED language reproduces the same estimates on identical rows
agreement._note: 1e-6 on the log-OR is far below any real effect and far above optimiser noise. A miss at this scale is a different model or a different default, never rounding.

recovery.claim: the estimate is close to the parameter the fixture actually used
_note: PROVISIONAL, and deliberately marked so. 0.45 is roughly three standard errors under a
back-of-envelope SE of about 0.15 for 400 matched sets at 35% exposure. Nothing here has run
the model, so the real SE is unmeasured. The FIRST CI run must report the observed standard
error and this tolerance must then be reset to a stated multiple of it. Leaving a guessed
tolerance in place would be a check calibrated against nothing.

must_appear._note: call sites codecheck.js can look for. Presence is not correctness: crr( being called says a competing-risks function was called, not that the right variable reached it.

sas.reason: no SAS engine licensed yet; see repository README on Altair SLC, which is SAS-language-compatible rather than SAS itself
